title: Blocks With a Sum Between Two Bounds, Negatives Allowed

concept.title: A block sum is a difference of two prefix sums, so count the earlier prefix sums that fall into a window
body: Count the blocks of neighbouring numbers whose sum is **at least `lo` and at most `hi`**. For `2 -1 3` with `lo = 1` and `hi = 3` the good blocks are `[2]`, `[3]`, `[2 -1]` and `[-1 3]`: the sums are 2, 3, 1 and 2, while `[-1]` and `[2 -1 3]` have the sums -1 and 4. With only positive numbers a sliding window could do it, but negative numbers break the monotonic behaviour of the sum.

Write the sum of the block `u+1 .. v` as `P[v] - P[u]` with the prefix sums `P[0] = 0`, `P[i] = a[1] + ... + a[i]`. The condition `lo <= P[v] - P[u] <= hi` becomes **`P[v] - hi <= P[u] <= P[v] - lo`**. So for every `v` we need the number of earlier prefix sums in a numeric window. Sort and compress all prefix sums to ranks, and keep a Fenwick tree with one count per rank.

body.code:
for v in pre:                                   # pre = P[0..n]
    first = bisect_left(vals, v - hi)           # ranks below the window
    last = bisect_right(vals, v - lo)           # ranks up to the window end
    total += bit_sum(t, last) - bit_sum(t, first)
    bit_add(t, bisect_left(vals, v) + 1, 1)     # now P[v] can be an earlier prefix sum

body: Because the count is taken before `P[v]` itself is inserted, only the pairs `u < v` are counted. Prefix sums reach `5 * 10^13`, so 64-bit numbers are needed, and the answer can be about `n^2 / 2`. Time O(n log n).

statement: A list of `n` numbers (possibly negative) is given. Count the blocks of neighbouring numbers (at least one number) whose sum is at least `lo` and at most `hi`. Blocks at different positions count separately, even if their numbers are equal. Print the count.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`, `lo` and `hi`: the length of the list and the two bounds.
The second line has the `n` numbers of the list.
outputFormat: Print one number: the count of blocks.

examples.note: The blocks [2], [3], [2 -1] and [-1 3] have the sums 2, 3, 1 and 2. The blocks [-1] and [2 -1 3] have the sums -1 and 4: 4.

hints: The sum of a block is a difference of two prefix sums.
For every end v you need the number of earlier prefix sums between P[v] - hi and P[v] - lo.
Compress the prefix sums and count the earlier ones in a Fenwick tree, using binary search to find the ends of the window.

explanation: Block sums are differences of prefix sums. For every prefix sum the earlier prefix sums that fall into the window [P[v] - hi, P[v] - lo] are counted with a Fenwick tree over the compressed values.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

def bit_add(t, i, x):
    n = len(t) - 1
    while i <= n:
        t[i] += x
        i += i & -i

def bit_sum(t, i):
    s = 0
    while i > 0:
        s += t[i]
        i -= i & -i
    return s

n, lo, hi = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

from bisect import bisect_left, bisect_right
pre = [0]
for x in a:
    pre.append(pre[-1] + x)
vals = sorted(set(pre))
t = [0] * (len(vals) + 1)
total = 0
for v in pre:
    first = bisect_left(vals, v - hi)
    last = bisect_right(vals, v - lo)
    total += bit_sum(t, last) - bit_sum(t, first)
    bit_add(t, bisect_left(vals, v) + 1, 1)
print(total)
